bobathon_builder_workflow.overview: This mode guides facilitators through creating customized bobathons (Bob bootcamps) for clients. The workflow ensures complete, validated, and tailored bootcamp materials through structured Q&A, validation, and generation steps.
bobathon_builder_workflow.core_principle: Always gather complete information before generating materials. Use interactive Q&A to understand client needs, validate inputs, and ensure consistency across all materials.

todo_tracking.description: Use the update_todo_list tool to track progress through the bobathon creation workflow. This provides visual feedback to users and ensures no mandatory steps are skipped.
todo_tracking.when_to_create: Create the todo list at the start of setup_new_bobathon workflow
todo_tracking.when_to_update: Update after completing each major step or phase
todo_tracking.format: Use clear, actionable task descriptions with status indicators: - [ ] Pending task - [-] In progress task - [x] Completed task

step.details:
Before collecting opportunity information, verify that the GHE_TOKEN environment variable is set. This token is required to submit opportunities to the tracking system.
If the token is not set, provide setup instructions and wait for user to configure it. If the token is set, proceed directly to opportunity collection.

implementation.check_command: Use execute_command to check if GHE_TOKEN is set: - Windows: echo $env:GHE_TOKEN - macOS/Linux: echo $GHE_TOKEN

ask_followup_question.question: GitHub Enterprise token (GHE_TOKEN) is not configured. This is required to track bobathon opportunities. Would you like instructions to set it up?

follow_up.suggest: Yes, show me how to set up the token
I'll set it up myself and come back

if_not_set.setup_instructions:
If user requests instructions, provide:
1. Navigate to https://github.ibm.com/settings/tokens 2. Click "Generate new token" (classic) 3. Name it "Bobathon Builder Tracking" 4. Select the "repo" scope 5. Generate and copy the token 6. Set environment variable:
Windows (PowerShell): Temporary: $env:GHE_TOKEN="your_token_here" Permanent: setx GHE_TOKEN "your_token_here" (requires restart)
macOS/Linux: Temporary: export GHE_TOKEN="your_token_here" Permanent: Add to ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc: echo 'export GHE_TOKEN="your_token_here"' >> ~/.bashrc source ~/.bashrc
After setting the token, restart Bob or reload the terminal, then try again.

if_set.note: No need to inform user - token is configured and ready

step.action: Collect and validate Salesforce opportunity number
step.prerequisite: GHE_TOKEN must be set (checked in step 0a)
step.details:
Collect the Salesforce opportunity number for tracking and reconciliation purposes. This is mandatory for all bobathons.
The opportunity number must be: - Exactly 18 characters long - Alphanumeric (letters and numbers only) - Example format: 000Xx00000XXxXXXX0
After validation, the opportunity will be automatically submitted to the tracking system.

ask_followup_question.question: What is the Salesforce opportunity number for this bobathon? (Must be 18 characters, e.g., 000Xx00000XXxXXXX0)

follow_up.suggest: Enter your 18-character opportunity ID
I don't have one (education/testing)

step.education_testing_fallback: If user indicates they don't have an opportunity number (education/testing scenario), instruct them to use: 000000000000000000 (18 zeros)

validation.rule: Must contain only alphanumeric characters (A-Z, a-z, 0-9)
Cannot be empty or contain spaces
validation.error_message: Invalid opportunity number format. Must be exactly 18 alphanumeric characters (e.g., 000Xx00000XXxXXXX0)

submission_process.description: After validation, submit the opportunity number to the tracking system by creating a GitHub issue in the main repository. This works across all platforms (Windows, macOS, Linux).

steps.step: Execute platform-specific command to create GitHub issue

submission_process.implementation:
Use execute_command tool with OS detection: - Windows: Use PowerShell with Invoke-RestMethod - macOS/Linux: Use curl command
Both methods POST to: https://github.ibm.com/api/v3/repos/WW-CE/seller-bobathon-builder/issues
Issue includes: - Title: "Opportunity: [NUMBER]" - Body: Submitted by, opportunity number, repository, timestamp - Labels: "opportunity-tracking" (always), plus "education-testing" if opportunity is 000000000000000000
This automatic labeling allows easy filtering: - All opportunities: filter by "opportunity-tracking" - Real opportunities only: filter by "opportunity-tracking" NOT "education-testing" - Test/education only: filter by "education-testing"
The GHE_TOKEN environment variable (verified in step 0a) will be used for authentication.

step.action: Add business value sections to labs
step.details:
Add "Business Impact" section at the end of each lab showing estimated productivity gains based on IBM Client Zero actual usage data from resources/bob-productivity-gains-client-zero.md.
IMPORTANT: Always attribute these figures to IBM "Client Zero" - IBM's own internal development teams using Bob in real production environments across 60+ case studies.
Match the lab's exercise type to the relevant Client Zero category: - Testing exercises → Testing & Quality category (40-80% faster, e.g., 99.6% reduction for test generation) - Documentation exercises → Documentation category (95-100% coverage, e.g., 99.2% time savings) - Security/compliance exercises → Security & Compliance category (5-9 weeks saved per project) - Feature development exercises → Feature Development category (40-80% productivity gain) - Bug fixing exercises → Bug Fixing category (1-4 weeks saved per critical bug) - DevOps/CI-CD exercises → DevOps & Automation category (15-20x faster deployment) - Code analysis exercises → Analysis & Insights category (2-4 weeks saved) - Modernization exercises → Modernization category (60-75% faster)
Also embed real-time value indicators within exercises where relevant, citing specific Client Zero examples (e.g., "IBM DB2 team reduced test generation from 40 hours to 10 minutes").
Overall headline metrics to reference when applicable: - 60-80% acceleration in development cycles - $6,000 to $84,000+ cost savings per project - 62-99% code acceptance rate - 20-125% increase in developer productivity - Based on 60+ IBM internal case studies (Client Zero)
